w10_P4_002601: A crane test sheet ends with one number in kilonewtons. A ballast block of mass 148 kg is driven along a rail. The drive must supply the force that gives that block that acceleration, and 25 N of it is lost in the guide rollers and subtracted. The sheet writes the remainder in kilonewtons, then adds 1 in those same kilonewton units as the standing offset. The rig's hydraulic pack holds 40 L of oil, which plays no part. What number ends the sheet, in kN?
w10_P4_002602: A cable-car works tests a carrier whose mass plate reads 193000 g. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger root of x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0. Twelve carriers run on the line, so the line demand is 12 times the logged value, and 11 is then added in those same kilonewton units for the drive-station tare. The station also has a 300 L water tank, which is not part of this. What is the final figure, in kN?
